🎯 Use BEM (Block__Element--Modifier) for class naming: .card, .card__title, .card--featured. It creates predictable, scalable CSS class names.

exercises.question: In BEM naming, which class name format represents a 'featured' modifier on a 'card' block?
exercises.explanation: BEM uses double hyphens for modifiers: block--modifier. Double underscores separate blocks from elements: block__element.

exercises.question: What WCAG level is considered the standard baseline that most organizations should target?
exercises.explanation: WCAG 2.1 AA is the internationally recognized baseline for accessibility compliance. Level A is too minimal; Level AAA is often impractical for all content.

sections.content: Performance Starts in HTML
HTML determines what loads, when it loads, and in what order. Smart HTML can cut seconds from your page load time without changing a single line of CSS or JavaScript.
💡 defer scripts execute in order after HTML parsing. async scripts execute as soon as downloaded — order is not guaranteed. Use defer for most scripts.

exercises.question: Which script loading attribute guarantees execution order AND doesn't block HTML parsing?
hints: async doesn't guarantee order; defer does
exercises.explanation: defer downloads scripts in parallel with HTML parsing and executes them in document order after parsing completes. async executes as soon as downloaded, which may be out of order.

sections.content: Build in Layers

Progressive enhancement is a development strategy: start with solid HTML that works everywhere, then add CSS for styling, then JavaScript for enhancement. Each layer enhances the previous but doesn't break it if the layer above fails.

<!-- Layer 1: HTML only — works without CSS or JS -->
<form action="/search" method="GET">
  <label for="q">Search</label>
  <input type="search" id="q" name="q" />
  <button type="submit">Search</button>
</form>
<!-- With CSS: beautifully styled
     With JS: real-time autocomplete suggestions
     Without JS: still a functioning search form
     Without CSS: ugly but works -->
💡 Progressive enhancement is especially important for users on slow networks, screen readers, or older devices. Your core content should always be accessible.

exercises.question: In progressive enhancement, what is the correct order of layers?
hints: Start with content, then style, then behaviour
exercises.explanation: HTML provides the semantic content baseline. CSS adds visual presentation. JavaScript adds interactive behaviour. Each layer degrades gracefully if disabled.
